text:
lia: seeing a spike in NCCL p2p failures on a subset of racks since the switch firmware roll last night. some jobs hit QP handshake timeouts and then retry, increasing latency.

sam: which racks/tor? any pattern by rev or SKU?

lia: euc2-gpu-rack-11 and -12 mostly. both on the new 3.2.1 image. not all pods, about 30% of multi-gpu jobs. single-gpu fine.

ops-bot: alert: job gpu-train-983 experienced nccl_peer_reset at 2201234569 (retries: 3). trace id: trc-7f2d.

kiran: can you paste the mlx logs from one affected host? especially QP creation errors and mlx5 driver messages.

lia: TL;DR logs: some QP create succeeds but later `IBV_EVENT_QP_FATAL` and timeouts to peer during RC handshake. snippet:``
Apr 07 03:02:11 host kernel: mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: mlx5_cmd_exec timeout
Apr 07 03:02:11 host kernel: ib_device 0000:05:00.0: failed to create qp, rc=-110
Apr 07 03:02:11 host kernel: IBV_EVENT_QP_FATAL on qp 0x7f9b3
``

mike: did we see any packet drops on the ToR? counters?

lia: ToR shows small TX bursts hit egress shaping. switch counters: `port 25: drop 137, tx-queue drop 21` around the same window.

sam: interesting — so not purely NIC bug. could be scheduling on the switch causing RDMA packets (RoCEv2) to be delayed and re-ordered enough to break the RC handshake before retry window.

kiran: what about MTU mismatches? any fragmentation logs?

lia: MTU consistent at 4096 across hosts and ToR. but I did notice a mismatch on a transit spine for one path where jumbo settings were accidentally left at 1500 after the firmware rolled over (spine-3). traffic for rack-11 was hairpinned via that spine for a short window during a maintenance move.

oncall-ryan: that could explain bursts and frag/reassembly overhead. RoCEv2 uses UDP; if frag occurs or ECN, packet timing gets weird. can we reproduce with `ibv_rc_pingpong` and `tcpdump -n -i any udp` to capture handshake packets?

lia: ran `ibv_rc_pingpong` between two GPUs on rack-11 while simulating the egress shaping on the ToR with `tc qdisc` — observed handshake timeouts when we introduce 200ms of queueing and a 1% drop.

mike: thanks, good repro. next steps: 1) roll back spine jumbo config and push 4096 everywhere, 2) coordinate with switch vendor on firmware scheduler delta, 3) temporarily route HPC racks via alternate spine to drain bursty paths.

sam: also add a short-term mitigation in the serving layer: bump NCCL_RETRY_TIMEOUT or fallback policy to use TCP for small control messages to reduce aborted handshakes. will that be safe?

kiran: we should avoid changing timeouts blindly; better to gate with a canary. add a per-rack routing policy + NCCL flag toggle for affected racks only.

lia: opened a change: `infra/changes/2201234575` rolling spine jumbo correction + emergency route for racks 11/12. vendor ticket #VND-3342 created with attached pcap and mlx logs.

ops-bot: change queued: infra/changes/2201234575 awaiting approvals from network and runtime teams.

oncall-ryan: I'll stay on the channel for the cutover. planning window in 15m. if anyone has quick commands to validate post-change: check `ethtool -S mlx5_core` for drop counters, `ibv_devinfo -v` for port state, and `nvidia-smi dmon` to watch GPU saturation during warmup.

lia: noted. will post results. initial repro and mitigation plan shared in the ticket. :thumbsup:

mike: follow-up: consider adding a periodic RDMA healthcheck job that does quick QP handshakes across racks and alerts when handshake latency > 100ms or failure > 1% for 5m. this would catch regressions earlier.

sam: yep + correlate with switch egress drops and queue depth via prometheus. I'll add an item to the infra backlog.

lia: post-cutover update (2201234595): after jumbo restore + reroute, affected jobs dropped from 30% failure to <1% within 5 minutes. QP fatal events ceased in the logs. still keeping vendor ticket open to root cause the scheduler change.

ops-bot: incident: resolved. incident-id inc-220123. duration 00:45.
